content.title: About
content.content: Danish pastry is a laminated sweet pastry made from a yeast‑leavened dough enriched with butter. The “plain” version is a buttery, flaky layer without filling, while the “spice” version incorporates aromatic spices such as cinnamon, cardamom, and ginger.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The pastry originated in 19th‑century Denmark, inspired by Austrian “Viennese” pastries.
Traditional lamination creates over 100 layers by repeatedly rolling and folding the dough.
In the United States the product is often simply called “pastry” or “Danish”.
There are more than 30 common fillings, ranging from fruit jams to almond cream and caramel.
In some Danish regions the pastry is served warm with milk as a breakfast staple.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Provides carbohydrates and a modest amount of fat for quick energy.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Yeast‑based dough supplies thiamine, riboflavin, and niacin, supporting metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidants (Spice version)
items.content: Spices like cinnamon and ginger contain polyphenols that may reduce oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Whole‑grain flour, when used, adds dietary fiber that aids bowel regularity.

items.title: Mood improvement
items.content: Carbohydrates promote serotonin production, which can enhance mood.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Fillings and sweetened dough can raise blood glucose levels.

items.title: Possible trans fats
items.content: Using margarine instead of butter may introduce trans fatty acids.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: Contains milk, eggs, gluten, and sometimes nuts, which can trigger allergies.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The buttery layers make the pastry calorie‑rich; moderation is advised.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy Danish pastry as a standalone treat, sliced and paired with coffee or tea. The spice‑infused version pairs especially well with hot milk or a scoop of vanilla ice cream.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in an airtight container at room temperature for 2‑3 days. For longer storage, refrigerate (up to 5 days) or freeze (up to 2 months). Reheat in the oven before serving to restore crispness.
